metadata.title: EXAMPLE (synthetic) — Extreme heat and all-cause mortality in metropolitan Phoenix, Arizona
metadata.citation_apa7: Example, A., & Sample, B. (2024). Extreme heat and all-cause mortality in metropolitan Phoenix, Arizona [Synthetic example record]. Journal of Arid Climate Health, 12(3), 200-215.

direct_exposures: Ambient extreme heat exposure (daily Tmax above the 95th percentile)

interventions.intervention_description: Evaluates the association between cooling-center accessibility and reduced heat-related mortality at the census-tract level.

q1_extreme_weather_health_impacts.summary: Days with maximum temperature above the local 95th percentile were associated with a measurable increase in all-cause mortality, concentrated in older and low-income populations.

q3_sustainable_solutions.summary: Greater cooling-center accessibility was associated with attenuated heat-mortality risk, suggesting a scalable adaptation.

associations_effects.effect_narrative: Each 1 degree C increase in daily Tmax above the 95th percentile was associated with a relative risk of all-cause mortality of RR = 1.04 (95% CI: 1.02-1.06).

correlations_table.variable: Daily Tmax (>95th pctile) vs all-cause mortality

vulnerable_populations.vulnerability_reasons: Reduced thermoregulation and higher prevalence of cardiovascular and renal conditions.
Prolonged occupational heat exposure and limited access to air conditioning.

climate_resilience.successful_adaptations: Census tracts with high cooling-center accessibility showed lower heat-attributable mortality, supporting cooling centers as an effective near-term adaptation.

relevance_summary: Synthetic example demonstrating a high-relevance heat-health study in an arid Southwest US city, exercising every section of the schema.

limitations_gaps.limitations: Ecological time-series design cannot establish individual-level causation; exposure misclassification from station-based temperature.
limitations_gaps.data_gaps: Lack of individual-level air-conditioning access data and sub-daily exposure timing.
limitations_gaps.future_research: Couple individual exposure monitoring with longitudinal cohorts and extend to climate projection scenarios.

overall_relevance.relevance_justification: Directly addresses extreme-heat health impacts and adaptation in an arid SW US metropolitan area, aligning with SCORCH objectives 1, 2, 4, and 6.

summary.paper_summary: Across 2010-2022 in Maricopa County (~4.5M residents), extreme-heat days were associated with a 4% per-degree increase in all-cause mortality (RR 1.04, 95% CI 1.02-1.06), with the burden concentrated among adults 65+ and low-income outdoor workers.
summary.conclusions_summary: Extreme heat is a significant and inequitable driver of mortality in arid Phoenix; expanding cooling-center access is associated with reduced risk and represents a viable adaptation.

extraction_metadata.notes: Synthetic record for pipeline/OKF demonstration and testing. Not derived from any real publication.
